summary.one_liner: mpi4py provides Python bindings for the Message Passing Interface (MPI) standard, letting Python programs use MPI for parallel and distributed computing.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes mpi4py as a package of Python bindings for the MPI standard, implemented on top of the MPI specification and exposing an API based on the MPI-2 C++ bindings. It requires Python 3.10 or newer (or PyPy 7.3 or newer) and an MPI implementation such as MPICH or Open MPI built with shared/dynamic libraries. The README points to Read the Docs and GitHub Pages documentation, plus mailing list and GitHub Discussions support. It also mentions an mpi4py.futures module for MPI-based asynchronous task execution, as described in its citation. The README does not show code examples or detailed feature lists in the text provided.
use_cases: run parallel Python jobs across multiple processes or nodes
send and receive messages between Python processes
use MPI from Python on HPC clusters
port MPI-based C or C++ scientific code to Python
how_to_run: Install an MPI implementation such as MPICH or Open MPI built with shared libraries
Install Python 3.10 or above, or PyPy 7.3 or above
Install mpi4py from its distribution (the README does not give the exact command in the provided text)
notable: Python bindings for the MPI standard, based on the MPI-2 C++ bindings API
Includes mpi4py.futures for MPI-based asynchronous task execution
Works with MPICH and Open MPI
caveats: Requires an MPI implementation built with shared/dynamic libraries installed separately
The provided README text contains no installation command or usage examples
